items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: Calloway going to pay you. ... He pay me.

ctx.x: But right away Chu Berry did like this. He was -- he was too much competition for him then. He was like a child. He said to me one day, I don't know why you bring this crazy son of a bitch in this band. They were already working Teddy Reath's band together. He don't want -- he don't want, say, man, I didn't brought him here. I just (inaudible) to play for me and (inaudible). I don't know why, what you got against this -- no, I don't got nothing against him, but you know what I mean. (Inaudible) this different…

All right. So Dizzy say, you know, one of these days this man going to start playing his tenor, and you going to look for his head, going to be in the middle of the floor, and the saxophone in the band. I said, don't do that. Don't pay no mind. Do your work and play your trumpet. Forget about it. He don't pay you. Calloway going to pay you.

So, well, it begin to develop, you know. All right. (inaudible) then Cab and me was like this. That they don't like. Some of the guys didn't like. (Inaudible) you always with Bauza, you know, (inaudible) drummer, say, I don't know what you call it, but I mean this man is the leader. He pay me. He
